Question 2(d) [4 marks]: Discuss the influence of globalisation on the operations function.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Defines globalisation and provides one advantage and one disadvantage
3 marks: Defines globalisation and provides a basic disadvantage and advantage
2 marks: No definition of globalisation, just gives one advantage OR disadvantage
1 marks: One advantage or disadvantage only


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Globalisation refers to the removal of barriers to trade between nations, creating a world economy. Advantages: cheaper foreign inputs (technology, raw materials); access to cheaper foreign labour by relocating manufacturing or service centres; access to foreign technology that increases efficiency, quality and speed; economies of scale from a larger global market. Disadvantages: increased competition from global firms puts pressure on costs or on differentiation; pressure to customise products for local tastes; exposure to exchange rate fluctuations when sourcing or selling overseas (hedging); exposure to different currencies, consumers, technology and cultures.
